record.paper_title: Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems
record.original_question: Find a proof based on Dulac functions showing that Lie(3) = 1 and Lie(4) = 1 for classical Liénard systems.

evidence.quote: Problem 4. Find a proof using Dulac functions that Lie(3) = 1 and Lie(4) = 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the classical Liénard differential system
  x' = y - F(x),    y' = -x,
where F is a real polynomial of degree n with F(0) = 0. For each integer n ≥ 1, let Lie(n) denote the maximum number of limit cycles (isolated periodic orbits) that such a system can have, taken over all polynomials F of degree exactly n. It is classically known that Lie(3) = 1 and Lie(4) = 1.

Recall that a Dulac function for a planar C^1 vector field X = (P, Q) on a simply connected open region U ⊂ R^2 is a C^1 function B : U → R such that the divergence
  div(B·X) = ∂(B P)/∂x + ∂(B Q)/∂y
does not change sign on U and is not identically zero on any open subset; the existence of such a B in U implies that X has no periodic orbit contained in U. (More generally, a Dulac–Cherkas function is a C^1 function Ψ together with a real number κ such that div(X) + κ·(X·∇Ψ)/Ψ has constant sign on U \ {Ψ = 0}.)

Problem. Provide a proof of the equalities Lie(3) = 1 and Lie(4) = 1 based on the explicit construction of Dulac (or Dulac–Cherkas) functions for the corresponding classical Liénard systems.
artifact.status_search_result: The values Lie(3) = 1 and Lie(4) = 1 are known (proved by Lins Neto–de Melo–Pugh and subsequent work), but the specific request to obtain these results via Dulac (or Dulac–Cherkas) functions appears not to have been carried out in the literature. Surveys on the Lins Neto–de Melo–Pugh conjecture and works on Dulac–Cherkas functions for generalized Liénard systems describe the method but do not supply such a Dulac-function-based proof of Lie(3) = Lie(4) = 1, so the problem appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Limit cycles of the classical Liénard differential systems: A survey on the Lins Neto, de Melo and Pugh's conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Survey on the Lins Neto–de Melo–Pugh conjecture about the maximum number of limit cycles of classical Liénard systems, including the established values Lie(3)=Lie(4)=1.
status_evidence.claim: The values Lie(3)=1 and Lie(4)=1 are known, but a Dulac-function-based proof is not provided.

status_evidence.title: Dulac–Cherkas functions for generalized Liénard systems
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of Dulac–Cherkas functions for generalized Liénard systems; for degree l ≥ 4 the construction requires solving an overdetermined system.
status_evidence.claim: Dulac–Cherkas constructions are available but no proof of Lie(3)=Lie(4)=1 via this method is given.
